title: Qman DirectPath host-snapshot publication repository transaction receipt
description: Closed V1 component receipt for one independently queried host-snapshot publication repository transaction. It binds the exact SERIALIZABLE transaction, four-authority CAS result, commit clock, mutation closure, persisted-after artifact hashes, write counts, target revision label, verifier nonce and verified trust context. It is deliberately component-only and does not authenticate a Qman target endpoint, prove a product database implementation, or close C00/G1.
x-qmanQueryDigestRule: queryDigest is SHA-256 over ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/HOST-SNAPSHOT-PUBLICATION-REPOSITORY-QUERY/V1), one zero byte, and CANONICAL-JSON-V1 of the closed query subject {repositoryId,transactionId,operationId,commandId,requestHash,operationRequestContextDigest,decisionContextDigest,mutationContextDigest,verificationNonce,targetRepositoryObjectFormat,targetRepositoryCommit,outcome,commitIdOrNull,repositoryTransactionCanonicalSha256,requestedAt,queryDigest:null}. verificationNonce is the unique unpadded base64url re-encoding of 16..64 decoded bytes; the schema excludes impossible length modulo four and the verifier rejects non-zero unused tail bits. The verifier supplies that fresh nonce, requestedAt and independently expected target revision; none may be learned only from the returned receipt.
x-qmanTrustBindingRule: canonicalProfileId, schemaRef and schemaSha256 exact-bind CANONICAL-JSON-V1, this fixed schema reference and the raw SHA-256 of the independently loaded schema document. trustContextDigest and every trustBinding field exact-project the same factory-verified trust context used to verify this receipt. Top-level keyRingSequence equals trustBinding.keyRingSequence. rootSetId/rootSetDigest/rootSetCanonicalSha256, keyRingId/keyRingSequence/keyRingDigest/currentKeyRingCanonicalSha256, trust-anchor identity/version/resourceVersion/digest/raw canonical SHA and live freshness receipt digest/expiry must also exact-match the operation request mutation read-set trust references. An alternate self-consistent root set, key ring, rollback anchor or copied expired freshness response is rejected.
x-qmanRepositoryTransactionBindingRule: repositoryTransactionCanonicalSha256 is SHA-256 of exact CANONICAL-JSON-V1 bytes of repositoryTransaction, which validates through directpath-host-snapshot-publication-trace.schema.json#/$defs/repositoryTransaction. Every duplicated repository/transaction/operation/command/request/context/outcome/commit/time/clock field is byte-equal. The transaction expectation and snapshotPublicationCasResult compare HostAuthority, global AvailabilityAuthority, capability-policy authority and freshness-policy authority in one SERIALIZABLE decision; expected versions, policy hashes, expectationHash, resolvedAuthorityVectorHash, mutationSetHashOrNull, commitRecordDigestOrNull and publicationMutationCount all exact-match their retained sources. Matching fields in this component receipt do not prove that a Qman product database performed that CAS.
x-qmanOutcomeClosureRule: COMMITTED has non-null commit ID/time, mutation-set and commit-record digests; snapshotPublicationCasResult.decision is COMMITTED; the four conditional raw wrapper hashes availabilityAuthorityAfterOrNull, auditRecordOrNull, outboxRecordOrNull and commitRecordOrNull are non-null; writeCounts are exactly 1 HostSnapshot, N DeviceRecords, 1 HostAuthority, 1 AvailabilityAuthority, 1 audit, 1 outbox and 1 commit record, where 1<=N<=4096 and publicationMutationCount=N+6. NO_CHANGE has null commit ID/time, mutation-set and commit-record digests, those same four conditional wrapper hashes null, snapshotPublicationCasResult.decision NO_CHANGE, publicationMutationCount zero and every write count zero. hostSnapshotAfter and hostAuthorityAfter always hash the exact selected persisted-after wrappers; mutationsCanonicalSha256 always hashes the exact canonical mutation array, including the canonical empty array for NO_CHANGE; deviceRecordSetDigest and resolvedAuthorityVectorHash remain non-null for both outcomes.
x-qmanCommitClockRule: All top-level clocks byte-equal repositoryTransaction. COMMITTED requires commitClockAfter=commitClockBefore+1 and observedAt is not before committedAtOrNull. NO_CHANGE requires commitClockAfter=commitClockBefore, committedAtOrNull is null, observedAt is not before repositoryTransaction.beganAt, and no repository write of any category occurred. Integer comparison is over the declared safe-integer range.
x-qmanDigestAndSignatureRule: After query, transaction, mutation, trust and time bindings pass, construct the complete closed receipt with receiptDigest and signature set to null. Let B be CANONICAL-JSON-V1 of that projection. Under the portable SIGNED-ENVELOPE-V1 profile, receiptDigest is SHA-256 of B with no domain prefix, and signature is Ed25519 over ASCII(QMAN-DIRECTPATH/HOST-SNAPSHOT-PUBLICATION-REPOSITORY-RECEIPT/V1), one zero byte, and that same B. Resolve signerKeyId through the exact trustBinding key ring and require the key to carry CONTROL_REPOSITORY_EVIDENCE, be active and be non-revoked at signedAt. requestedAt <= observedAt <= signedAt <= verifier time and signedAt <= trustBinding.trustFreshnessExpiresAt. The null/null construction projection need not validate as a stored signed receipt.
x-qmanAcyclicConstructionRule: The dependency direction is verified operation request and trust context -> publication decision/rollback preparation -> repository transaction and commit rows -> mutation context -> fresh repository query -> this receipt. queryDigest points to the prior mutation/transaction context; this receipt points one-way to queryDigest and prior digests. receiptDigest, signature, queryDigest and any result/context/trace/Case/evidence-index digest are forbidden from the repository commit record or mutation-set preimage, preventing a fixed point or post-commit digest back-reference.
x-qmanAuthorityBoundary: This schema and a valid component signature prove only deterministic closure over supplied canonical bytes and the signer identity resolved through the supplied factory-verified trust context. They do not authenticate a target transport, prove endpoint/session/controller identity, demonstrate a mapped Qman SERIALIZABLE/SSI implementation, establish crash durability or independent visibility, authorize product use, close C00/G1, or upgrade evidence beyond component-only without separately mapped target code and product execution evidence.
